items.title: Scalability: ek user ke liye fast, das lakh ke liye nahi
items.one_idea: Scalability means a system keeps working well as the load grows; one server that is fast for a single user hits a limit (its slowest resource), so the real question is what grows when load grows.
items.spoken_hook: Interviewer ने पूछा: 100 users पर चलने वाला app, 10 लाख पर क्यों टूटता है?
items.hook_10s: Interviewer ने पूछा: 100 users पर चलने वाला app, 10 लाख पर क्यों टूटता है? जवाब ये है: app वही रहता है, पर हर user थोड़ा काम माँगता है, और काम जोड़ने पर कोई एक चीज़ पहले भर जाती है। [frame 0: one server box with 3 tiny user dots, calm; then the dots multiply into a crowd at its door]

items.hook_source: hook-writer interviewer_asked; the topic is the Wikipedia definition of scalability https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scalability
items.visual_idea: One server box drawn with three small bars inside (CPU, memory, disk). A few user dots send requests and the bars barely move; the dots grow to a crowd and the weakest bar fills to the top first and turns the box into the stuck point while the other bars stay half empty. Then a second copy of the box appears and the crowd splits between the two, and every bar drops.
items.everyday_anchor: A chai stall that serves 5 friends smoothly but jams at the college gate at 5 pm when 500 students arrive, because one stove and one cashier cannot grow with the crowd.
items.example: EXAMPLE (invented numbers, arithmetic shown): one server handles 100 requests per second; 100 users sending 1 request each per 10 seconds is 10 requests per second, so it is 10 percent busy. 10 lakh users at the same rate is 10,00,000 / 10 = 1,00,000 requests per second, which is 1,000 times the limit. Scaling means this gap is closed by adding capacity (more servers, or a bigger one), not by hoping the code is fast.
facts_to_verify: Scalability = property of a system to handle a growing amount of work, in software often by adding resources (Wikipedia Scalability).

A bottleneck is the point where one component caps the whole system's performance (Wikipedia Bottleneck (software)); the AWS page only supports that AWS has a performance efficiency pillar, claim nothing more from it.
Adding hardware can have diminishing returns (Wikipedia Scalability, Amdahl's law): say it in one line as the catch, no numbers.
The 100 requests per second limit and all user counts are EXAMPLE; recompute 10,00,000 / 10 = 1,00,000 and the 1,000x ratio.
Do not claim any real company's numbers; horizontal vs vertical is only named, not taught (that is its own day).
